0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part X ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 13 November 1980, after the draft finalized by the Gas Cylinders Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council.
0.2 For safe handling of cylinders containing liquid methyl bromide one should be thoroughly conversant with the properties and characteristics of and safe practices which methyl bromide. Th ere are several precautions are to be observed on account of the nature of the methyl bromide and also because of the pressure to which the cylinders are subjected. 0.3 Manufacturers, fillers, and users of the gas cylinders code should be familiar with the precautions laid down order to ensure safe and efficient operating conditions. formation on different gases conveyed in cylinders, SP also be referred to. 0.4 For different the purpose of parts as under: ( Part easy reference the standard covered by this in this code in For general in: g-1973' may issued in

0.5 The precautions to be observed for ensuring safety in the use of these cylinders have been classified under the following headings: a) General properties of methyl bromide; guidance for manufacture; b) Approved c) Inspection; d) Testing; e) Fitting; f ) Filling; g) Marking h) j) Storage; Handling; and precautions. and labelling; specifications and general

k) Transportation; m) General

0.6 Manufacture, possession and use of any gas when contained in cylinders in a compressed or liquefied form is regulated under the Gas Cylinder Rules, 1940, of the Government of India as amended from time to time. Although the code has been prepared in consultation and agreement with the statutory authorities under these rules, should anything in 4

0.7 The quantities in this standard have been expressed in technical metric units. However, in view of the introduction of International System ( SI ) units in the country, the relevant SI units and the corresponding conversion factors are given below for guidance: 1 kgf/cms = 98.066 5 kPa ( kilopascal ) = 0.980 665 bar

0.8 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 0.9 In using this code, mind. requirements of IS : 1312-1967t shall be borne in

4.

APPROVED SPECIFICATIONS FOR MANUFACTURE

AND

GENERAL

GUIDANCE

4.1 The cylinders

shall conform to one of the specifications approved by statutory authority. A list of approved ~specifications for filling in this country is given in Appendix A. _

4.2 Cylinders manufactured in accordance with approved specifications shall be provided with an additional wall thickness to allow for corrosion during service. It shall be brone in mind that corrosion is not related to the thickness of the container so that any additional thickness allowed for corrosion should be constant rather than a given proportion of thickness. 4.3 Further additional wall thickness shall also be considered necessary in order that the cylinder can safely withstand stresses due to horizontal acceleration and retardation in normal road transportation. The cylinder

IS I 8198 ( Part X ) - 1980 shall be so designed that the maximum permissible equivalent stress will not be exceeded when the stresses in the cylinder due to vertical accelerations are superimposed upon the stress due to internal pressure. The vertical accelerations considered should be those occurring in normal The provisions to be made in these and other respects as road transport. well as manufacturing tolerances to be applied will generally be decided between the user and rhe manufacturer. If a pronounced departure from normal practice is proposed or if other unusual features arise, the statutory authority shall be consulted.

9.2 Labelling 9.2.1 Each cylinder filled shall carry a label tacked to it detailing the name of the filling station, its location, name of gas in bold capital ` METHYL BROMIDE ' and its grade, net weight and warning instructions as stipulated in Gas Cylinder Rules, 1940 as amended from time to time.
9.2.2 The minimum cautionary notice shall be worded as under:

WARNING DANGEROUSLY HAZARDOUS UNDER ALL CONDITIONS, ALWAYS STORE, UNDER LOCK AND KEY. WEAR RUBBER GLOVES, PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND -RESPIRATOR WHILE FUMIGATING. 9.2.3 The containers shall also be marked with the symbols of danger of non-flammable compressed gases and for danger of poisoning as specified in IS : 1260 ( Part I )-1973*. The cylinder shall also be marked with poison lable as given in Fig. 3 of IS : 1260 ( Part I )-1973*. 10.

11. HANDLING 11.1 The
gas shall be called only by its name. so that these

11.2 Adequate care shall be taken in handling the cylinders are not dropped or struck against each other violently.

11.3 Cylinders shall be moved on properly balanced hand trucks, preferably with rubber tyres. A clamp or chain support two-thirds of the way up the cylinder shall be used. 11.4 Hoisting of cylinders is not recommended. However, if hoisting cannot be avoided, a lifting clamp cradle or carrier shall always be used. Cylinders shall never be hoisted with lifting magnet, rope or chain sling. A cylinder shall never be lifted by the hoods as it is not strong enough to support the weight. 11.5 The cylinders shall not be used as rollers colour and of to move cylinders shall other equipment. shall
